title: JWT Decoder
description: Decode JWT header and payload in the browser, inspect claims, dates, and security warnings without sending the token to the server.
metaDescription: Decode JWT header and payload in the browser, inspect claims, dates, and security warnings without sending the token to the server.

form.title: Decode JWT
form.description: Paste a compact JWT to inspect header, payload, claims, and dates without signature verification.

input.title: JWT token
input.label: Compact JWT
input.placeholder: Paste a JWT as header.payload.signature or Bearer header.payload.signature
input.privacy: Decoding happens in your browser. This tool does not send the token to the server or save history.
input.warning: JWTs can be active bearer credentials. Avoid pasting production tokens unless you understand the risk.

share.title: Share
share.description: The shared link points only to this tool route.
share.safe: Token, header, and payload never enter the link, query string, or fragment.

result.title: Result
result.description: The tool decodes, but does not validate signature, issuer, audience, revocation, or authorization.
result.emptyDescription: Paste a compact JWT to see header, payload, and claims.
result.validDescription: Header and payload were decoded, but the signature was not verified.
result.unsupportedJweDescription: The protected header was read when possible, but a JWE payload is encrypted and requires decryption outside this tool.
result.invalidDescription: Fix the structure, Base64URL, UTF-8, JSON, or claim shape and try again.
result.tooLargeDescription: The automatic limit is {limit} characters to avoid browser freezes.

errors.title: Diagnostic
errors.inputTooLarge: The input exceeds this tool size limit.
errors.emptyBearerToken: The Bearer prefix was provided without a token.
errors.internalWhitespace: The input contains spaces or line breaks inside the compact JWT.
errors.invalidPartCount: A compact JWT/JWS must have 3 parts; compact JWE has 5 parts.
errors.invalidBase64urlCharacter: The {part} part contains characters outside Base64URL.
errors.invalidBase64urlPadding: The {part} part has Base64URL padding in an invalid position or count.
errors.invalidBase64urlLength: The {part} part has a length that is invalid for Base64URL.
errors.invalidUtf8: The {part} part does not decode to valid UTF-8 text.
errors.invalidJson: The {part} part does not contain valid JSON.
errors.invalidHeaderShape: The header must be a JSON object.
errors.invalidPayloadShape: The payload must be a JSON object for JWT claim interpretation.

descriptions.iss: Issuer: identifies the issuing system, without proving trust by itself.
descriptions.sub: Subject: identifies the subject within the issuer context.
descriptions.aud: Audience: expected recipient, as a string or list.
descriptions.exp: Expiration time: NumericDate in UTC seconds.
descriptions.nbf: Not before: instant before which the token should not be accepted.
descriptions.iat: Issued at: instant when the token declares it was issued.
descriptions.jti: JWT ID: unique identifier whose meaning depends on the issuer.

time.title: NumericDate values
time.empty: No exp, nbf, or iat claim was found.

seoDetails.title: How to read the result
seoDetails.decodeDescription: Compact JWT exposes header and payload encoded as Base64URL. Seeing those values does not prove signature, origin, or permission.
seoDetails.verifyDescription: This version does not fetch JWKS, accept a secret, run cryptographic validation, or perform OAuth introspection.
seoDetails.claimsDescription: exp, nbf, and iat are NumericDate seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. iss, sub, aud, and jti depend on issuer policy.

privacy.question: Is the token sent to the server?
privacy.answer: Not by this tool. Processing happens in the browser and the shared link does not include token, header, or payload.

verification.question: Does decoding a JWT validate the signature?
verification.answer: No. Decoding only reads Base64URL and JSON. The correct application still needs to verify signature, issuer, audience, time, and policy.

parts.question: What do header, payload, and signature mean?
parts.answer: Header describes JOSE metadata, payload carries visible claims, and signature is cryptographic material that this tool does not verify.

numericDate.question: How should I interpret exp, nbf, and iat?
numericDate.answer: They are NumericDate values: seconds since the Unix epoch in UTC. The interface shows UTC ISO and a local reading for checking.

algNone.question: Why is alg=none dangerous?
algNone.answer: alg=none indicates a JWT without a signature. Common systems should not accept it unless they were explicitly designed and validated for that case.

jwe.question: Why can I not decode a JWE?
jwe.answer: JWE is encrypted. Without decryption keys, only the protected header can be inspected safely.

sharing.question: Can I share a prefilled JWT?
sharing.answer: This first version does not create links with a prefilled JWT. Copying JSON, screenshots, or pasting the token manually can still expose credentials.

seo.about: The JWT Decoder separates compact tokens into parts, decodes header and payload with Base64URL and UTF-8, formats JSON, and shows registered claims. It also identifies compact JWE as unsupported to avoid confusing encoding with decryption.
seo.howToUse: Paste a compact JWT or a value with a Bearer prefix, review header, payload, claims, and warnings, and copy only the pieces you need. Default sharing copies only the tool URL, without token content.
